Changed images may also be served stale for up to 30 days, so a missing or mismatched asset would be unverified rather than a content defect.

Source support unverified. specs/content/efpg-401/sources/texts/daulay-2025-listening.md, hartati-2024-reading.md and yunus-2013-writing.md are author paraphrases with a title-only passage anchor and state that they are not a substitute for independent source review, so the claims resting on them (topic-01.mdx:76, topic-03.mdx:55, topic-04.mdx:58) could not be checked against the actual passages. The three print monographs are declared under ## Unverifiable sources per D-2026-0001, which is honest, but their specific in-text attributions remain unverified.

docs/semester-3/efpg-401/unit-01/unit-assessment.mdx:32-93: the MCQ answer key is unbalanced, with 8 of 10 items keyed B (items 1-7 and 9) and only items 8 and 10 keyed C. A key this skewed is guessable. Recommend rebalancing option order across all four choices, as was done for Unit 5.

docs/semester-3/efpg-401/unit-01/topic-03.mdx:75 says "Teachers must train primary pupils in four primary reading sub-skills" but then lists five: skimming, scanning, intensive reading, extensive reading and inferential reading. static/img/figures/efpg-401/unit-01/fig-U1-6.svg and specs/content/efpg-401/coverage/unit-01.md show four lenses. Reconcile the count with the list and the figure.

Specific claims are attributed to the three title-level monographs: Cook (1991) on comprehensible input at topic-01.mdx:39; Celce-Murcia (1991) on segmental and suprasegmental features at topic-02.mdx:49, on the interactive reading model at topic-03.mdx:71 and on functional writing at topic-04.mdx:109; Nolasco and Arthur (1987) on turn-taking at topic-02.mdx:68. specs/content/efpg-401/sources/unit-01.md declares these works as title-level support and names the use areas, so the limitation is disclosed, but the claims are not verified. Consider narrowing the wording to the declaration or recasting the guidance as the unit's own, as Unit 5 was repaired.
